entry_points.text: A disease affects ●1 of a population. A test for it has ●2 sensitivity and ●3 specificity. If a randomly chosen person tests positive, what is the probability they actually have the disease?

params.description: the prevalence of the disease in the population as a percentage with unit (the fraction of the population that has the disease)
params.validity_range: Strictly between 0% and 100%. At 0% or 100% the disease is absent or universal, so P(disease | positive) is undefined or trivial. Values must be non-negative.

params.description: the sensitivity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person with the disease tests positive)
params.validity_range: Between 0% and 100% inclusive. Sensitivity of 0% makes P(+) depend only on false positives; the posterior is still defined provided P(+) > 0.

params.description: the specificity of the test as a percentage with unit (the probability that a person without the disease tests negative)
params.validity_range: Between 0% and 100% inclusive. Specificity of 100% gives zero false positives; the posterior is undefined only if P(+) = 0, which requires sensitivity 0% together with specificity 100%.

entry_points.text: A buffer is made by dissolving ●2 ●1 and ●4 ●3 in water to make ●5 of solution. Ka for ●1 is ●6. What is the pH after ●7 is added?

params.description: the name of the weak acid HA that forms the buffer
params.validity_range: Must be a named weak monoprotic acid with a defined Ka between 0 and 1 (exclusive), so that it partially dissociates and forms a buffer with its conjugate base. Strong acids (e.g. HCl) or non-acids are invalid for this class.

params.description: the amount in moles of the weak acid HA with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite number of moles (greater than 0). Zero would mean no buffer exists.

params.description: the name of the salt that supplies the conjugate base A- of the weak acid
params.validity_range: Must be a salt whose anion is the conjugate base of the weak acid in ●1 and whose cation is spectator (fully soluble, no acid-base contribution). Must not be a different acid's conjugate base.

params.description: the amount in moles of the conjugate base A- supplied by the salt with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite number of moles (greater than 0). Both acid and base must be present in nonzero amounts for the Henderson-Hasselbalch treatment to apply.

params.description: the total volume of the buffer solution with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite volume. Since HA and A- share this volume, it cancels in the mole ratio, but it must be positive so the solution exists.

params.description: the acid dissociation constant Ka of the weak acid HA (dimensionless, in scientific notation)
params.validity_range: Must be a positive number strictly less than 1 (weak acid regime). Values far outside typical weak acid range (roughly 1e-12 to 1e-1) would make the acid not behave as a weak buffer component.

params.description: the amount in moles and identity of the strong acid added to the buffer (HCl)
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative amount of a strong acid that fully dissociates (e.g. HCl, HBr, HNO3). The Henderson-Hasselbalch result is valid only while added moles are less than the moles of conjugate base (●4); beyond that the conjugate base is exhausted and the buffer no longer applies.

entry_points.text: A ●1 bond with a ●2 face value pays a ●3 annual coupon in ●4 installments. If the market yield is ●5 (annual, compounded ●6), what is the bond's price?

params.description: the time to maturity of the bond in years, with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive duration in years. Non-integer values are allowed but the number of periods n = years times payments per year must come out as a positive number; very large values only make the discount factor small and do not break the formula.

params.description: the face value (par value) of the bond with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a strictly positive monetary amount. A face value of zero would make the bond worthless as a claim and is outside the meaningful range.

params.description: the annual coupon rate of the bond as a percentage of face value
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative percentage. A value of 0% is valid and corresponds to a zero-coupon bond, where the coupon term vanishes. Values above roughly 100% are economically implausible but the formula still computes.

params.description: the frequency of coupon installments per year, as a payment schedule word
params.validity_range: Must map to a positive integer number of payments per year: annual = 1, semiannual = 2, quarterly = 4, monthly = 12. Other integer frequencies are logically valid but uncommon.

params.description: the annual market yield (required return) on the bond as a percentage
params.validity_range: Must be greater than -100% so that the periodic growth factor 1 + i is positive, which is required for the discounting formula to be defined. Practically it is a positive percentage; a yield equal to the coupon rate gives a par bond, a yield above the coupon rate gives a discount bond, and below gives a premium bond.

params.description: the compounding frequency of the market yield as a schedule word
params.validity_range: Must map to a positive integer number of compounding periods per year: annually = 1, semiannually = 2, quarterly = 4, monthly = 12. It determines the periodic yield i = annual yield divided by this integer, and should normally match the coupon frequency so the periods align.

entry_points.text: In how many ways can ●1 people be seated around a round table if two particular people, ●2 and ●3, refuse to sit next to each other?

params.description: the total number of distinct people to be seated around the round table, as a positive integer count

params.validity_range: Positive real currency amount; must be strictly greater than the salvage value (●2), otherwise there is no depreciable base and the book value is trivially the cost.

params.validity_range: Non-negative currency amount, and strictly less than the original cost (●1); a salvage value of zero is allowed and simply removes the floor.

params.validity_range: Positive integer number of years, at least 2 so that the DDB rate 2/n does not exceed 1 (n=1 would imply a rate of 200%, which is meaningless beyond the salvage floor).

params.description: the depreciation method to apply, which must be double-declining-balance depreciation
params.validity_range: Must denote the double-declining-balance method (rate equal to twice the straight-line rate 1/n applied to beginning book value); other methods such as straight-line or sum-of-years-digits require different calculations and are outside this template.

params.validity_range: Non-negative integer year index, from 0 (cost itself, unchanged book value) up to the useful life (●3); beyond the useful life the asset is fully depreciated and the book value equals the salvage value.

entry_points.text: In a population of ●1 people, ●2 have ●3, a ●4 condition. Assuming Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, how many people are expected to be carriers?

params.description: the total population size N (count of individuals in the population)
params.validity_range: Must be a positive integer (N ≥ 1) and at least as large as the affected count in ●2. Very small N gives coarse frequency estimates but is still valid.

params.description: the number of individuals showing the recessive phenotype (homozygous recessive count) with the condition
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative integer no greater than the total population size in ●1. Zero affected gives q = 0 and no carriers; a count equal to N is impossible for a recessive trait in equilibrium with carriers.

params.description: the name of the genetic condition or trait
params.validity_range: Any non-empty name of a trait; it is a label only and does not change the calculation.

params.description: the inheritance mode of the condition (must be recessive for carrier counting)
params.validity_range: Only a recessive mode is valid for this method. Dominant inheritance has no heterozygous carriers defined this way, so the calculation does not apply to it. Autosomal recessive is the standard case assumed by the 2pq formula.

entry_points.text: Demand is ● 1 and supply is ● 2. A ● 3 per-unit tax is imposed on sellers. What is the new price buyers pay, and what is the deadweight loss?

params.description: The linear demand curve expressing quantity demanded Q as a function of price P (intercept and slope)
params.validity_range: Must be a linear demand equation in Q and P with a negative price slope (quantity demanded falls as price rises) and a positive quantity intercept, so that a positive equilibrium price and quantity exist; slope must be nonzero.

params.description: The linear supply curve expressing quantity supplied Q as a function of price P (intercept and slope)
params.validity_range: Must be a linear supply equation in Q and P with a positive price slope (quantity supplied rises with price) so that supply and demand intersect at a positive price and quantity; the intercept must make the pre-tax equilibrium quantity positive.

params.description: The per-unit tax amount charged on each unit sold, in dollars, levied on sellers
params.validity_range: Must be a nonnegative dollar amount per unit; a tax of zero yields no change, and a tax large enough that the post-tax equilibrium quantity would be zero or negative (the market shuts down) is outside the regime where the standard triangle deadweight loss formula applies.

entry_points.text: A sample of ●1 bolts has a mean length of ●2 and a sample standard deviation of ●3. At ●5, test whether the true mean length differs from ●4. Give the test statistic and your conclusion.

params.description: the sample size n, the number of observations in the sample
params.validity_range: Must be an integer of at least 2, so that degrees of freedom n-1 is at least 1; larger n gives a more precise standard error, and very small n makes the t critical values large.

params.description: the sample mean of the measured quantity with its unit
params.validity_range: Any real number in the same unit as the hypothesized mean and the standard deviation; no sign restriction for a general measured quantity, but the unit must match the hypothesized mean.

params.description: the sample standard deviation of the measured quantity with its unit
params.validity_range: Must be strictly positive (greater than 0); a zero standard deviation would make the t statistic undefined, and it must be expressed in the same unit as the sample mean.

params.description: the hypothesized population mean under the null hypothesis, with its unit
params.validity_range: Any real number in the same unit as the sample mean; it is the value tested in the null hypothesis H0 that the true mean equals it.

params.description: the significance level alpha for the two-tailed test
params.validity_range: Must lie strictly between 0 and 1; conventional values are 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10, and smaller alpha gives larger critical values and a stricter rejection rule.

entry_points.text: A ball is launched from the top of a ●1 cliff at ●2, ●3 above the horizontal. Taking g = ●4, how far from the base of the cliff does it land?

params.description: the height of the cliff above its base, with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite length (height > 0). A height of zero reduces to ground-level launch, which is a degenerate case; negative heights (launch point below the base) are not in the class as described.

params.description: the launch speed of the ball, with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite speed (v0 > 0). Speed zero means no motion and no landing distance, so it is excluded.

params.description: the launch angle of the ball measured above the horizontal, with unit
params.validity_range: Angle in the open interval (-90°, 90°) for a nonzero forward range. 0° is a horizontal launch and is valid; negative angles mean launch below horizontal and are valid. ±90° (straight up or straight down) gives zero horizontal displacement and is a degenerate case.

params.description: the gravitational acceleration magnitude, with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite acceleration magnitude (g > 0), taken as downward. Values near 9.8 m/s² correspond to Earth; any positive value gives a valid instance of the same class.

entry_points.text: A simply supported steel beam spans ●1 and carries a uniform load of ●2. With modulus of elasticity ●3 and second moment of area ●4, what is the maximum deflection?

params.description: the span length L of the simply supported beam with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite length with a length unit; physically meaningful spans are roughly 0.1 m to a few hundred metres. A zero or negative span is invalid.

params.description: the uniform load intensity w acting over the full span of the beam with unit
params.validity_range: Non-negative force per unit length with a force-per-length unit. Zero gives zero deflection; the linear-elastic formula holds only while the beam stays elastic and the load is within the design range.

params.description: the modulus of elasticity E of the beam material with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive stress unit value. Typical structural values are roughly 1 GPa to 500 GPa (steel about 200 GPa). Zero or negative is physically invalid.

params.description: the second moment of area I of the beam cross-section with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive length-to-the-fourth unit value. Realistic beam sections give roughly 10⁻⁸ m⁴ to 10⁻² m⁴. Zero or negative is invalid because the section must have area.
